quest.title: Cards Out! Grievances Begone
quest.description: These duels are once in a century! Each table is a storm of activity, and old grudges will be settled on this day!
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Invokation Coupons x100, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

talks.objective: Go to Ritou to investigate the Card Snatcher

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, look! Promo posters everywhere, from the moment you arrive in the harbor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon gets more and more curious about the two inventors of this game every time we see the posters.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You're not the only one. There's so little information to go off of that there's all sorts of wild speculations about them.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Some people say that they invented the game after the God of Wisdom gave them an epiphany, while others say that they're not actually the inventors at all...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: By the way, have you two ever read a book called King of Invokations?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Well, it's a story about a young boy who gets possessed by the spirit of the Crocodile King and becomes a TCG player. It's quite fascinating. I made sure to read it before coming on this trip.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Some people have even speculated that the author of King of Invokations is the boy who was possessed, while the true inventors of the game are the Crocodile King and Ibis King from the legends...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Each of these theories gets more ridiculous than the last...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Exactly, which is why the original author came forward to deny these rumors.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But that only fueled the debate further, and the book's sales skyrocketed.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: It can't be denied that the King of Invokations novels are a major part of why Genius Invokation TCG has become so popular.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Just look at the venue, they're almost treating this like a national festival. I bet the book is going to sell more copies after this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, you can be sure that the fox lady is behind all this.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Fox lady?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Yae Miko! She's chief editor of the Yae Publishing House. Paimon can just imagine her eating some Fried Tofu as she instructs her editors to use this event to boost light novel sales.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Ah yes, I've been in that situation many times myself. Although in our case, the boss would be drinking coffee and talking about newspaper sales...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like bosses are the same everywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: The scenery in every nation is so different. This trip is really paying dividends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good thing that you're able to be so optimistic about it. It sounded like you were pretty much forced to come on this trip whether you wanted to or not...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, is that who Paimon thinks it is? It's Ei!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, who is this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, allow Paimon to introduce you... Huh, seems like that's all Paimon's been doing these past few days...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, this is Charlotte. She's a journalist from Fontaine. And this is Ei, she's, uh... She's Inazuma's archon.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: WHAT!? Y—You mean... Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder!? Ah, h—hello! Please forgive me for not recognizing you, I...!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: As a guest from afar, there's no need to be so formal.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Right, uh... I mean, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Whew, each of your acquaintances is more impressive than the last.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Miko invited me here to experience the fun and festivities along with everybody else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it. The tournament venue is full of excitement and tasty food, and Miko didn't want you to miss out.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I... guess I'll let you catch up for now. We can meet up later, just like last time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing. See ya, Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Perhaps she felt a little intimidated by me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's probably fine. Don't worry, she didn't leave because of you, we've split up like this in the previous places we've visited, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, how do you like Genius Invokation TCG? Paimon bets you're enjoying watching the tournament matches.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Well... In fact, I myself am competing in the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, really!?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Why is that surprising? Playing cards is an ancient form of entertainment, and I was curious to see what card games are like in this day and age.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the tournament been?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I advanced all the way to the semifinals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The semifinals? That's amazing! So when's your next match?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, the semifinals is where my journey ended. The reason being...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The reason being that she lost to me. And when I say "lost," that doesn't begin to do it justice. It was quite a humiliating defeat.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, I'll pretend I didn't hear that.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I only lost because I was duped by her little tricks.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: What's wrong with my little tricks? Trickery within the scope of the rules is better known as ingenuity. It's not my fault that some people spend all their time cooped up in Tenshukaku and never have the chance to hone their skills.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a unique friendship...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Huh... You're right, though. I should make an effort to get out more.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Many things have changed now that Inazuma is at peace. However... it seems that some people continue to fear the "divine light" just as before.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: In some of my tournament matches, I could see my opponent's hands shaking, hesitant to play their cards. Now that I think about it, perhaps they were scared of what would happen if they defeated me...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *yawn* Dear, dear. Other players lose their games and throw a tantrum... You win yours, and yet you still find a reason to mope about it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I invited you out for some simple fun and games... *sigh* I should have known you'd be like this.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Anyway, you should watch and learn, because I plan on using some more of my "little tricks" to defeat that Divine Priestess from Watatsumi Island.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? So Kokomi's your opponent in the finals?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Mm-hmm. On one side will be your erstwhile comrade in arms, the leader of Watatsumi Island, and on the other will be head shrine maiden Yae Miko, the wise and beautiful. So, little one, who will you support?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hah, the nerve, saying that in the presence of me and Ei! Are you trying to find out whose lightning strikes faster?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Miko, come on... no need to put them on the spot like that.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, I know. I just wanted to see how they'd react.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The venue is right over there. Why not go and take a walk around? Oh, and if you meet my fellow finalist, do pass on my regards.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Good choice.

talks.objective: Go to the Ritou competition venue and look for Kokomi

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, compadre! And Flying Lavender Melon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grr, Bull-chucker! Don't call Paimon that in public!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hahaha! What would this tournament be without Arataki "The Ultimate TCG Champion" Itto!?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Matter of fact, the whole Arataki Gang showed up in force. Our goal? To bring home the grand prize!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: And as fate would have it, Boss was the only one who didn't make it out of the qualifiers.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: H—Hey! That's not the point. It was just some bad luck, that's all. I got matched against a strong opponent in the first round!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Besides, it was a close match. It could have swung either way!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I wouldn't exactly call losing in three rounds a close match.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey, Shinobu! Cut me some slack in front of my friends, okay? Anyway, it's not like you did much better! Weren't you beaten by that fish lady... Sandy Mamma-Mia... whatever her name was?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Sangonomiya Kokomi? Watatsumi Island's military strategist? Yes, she beat me fair and square. I don't have a problem with that.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Pfft, well anyway, I've noticed something in this competition. If you wanna win big here, you need style. That's right, I'm talkin' card backs! I lost my match 'cause mah backs were wack!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the style of card backs and a player's skill don't have anything to do with each other.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Oh, no no no no! That's where you're wrong, mini melon.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: It's just like how the strongest Onikabuto have the brightest colors on their back. If your cards look cool, then you'll definitely draw a better hand!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Boss, beetle fighting and playing TCGs are completely different. In cards, you actually have to rely on your own skill.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Yeah, there's no use arguing with you... Why don't we let our friend here weigh in, hmm?

choices.text: I think Shinobu has a point...

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: #See? {M#He}{F#She} agrees.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Alright, that's it, I know how to settle this. We're gonna play a match right now, you and me!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: How 'bout this... Shinobu, lend me your deck. You've got some pretty slick card backs.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: #Hmm, but {NICKNAME} probably has cool card backs, too... maybe even better than yours. Okay, in that case, you can use my deck!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Boss, how do I put this... Nobody could win with that deck of yours. No matter who uses it...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hey! Quit bustin' my chops, sheesh! Whaddya say, Traveler? You got time for a match now?

choices.text: Actually, I think Itto has a point...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: See, I knew you'd understand!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: And you know what, since you're here — let's play a match to prove I'm right!

choices.text: Why don't we play a match and see...?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: ...Hey, you're right! That's a pretty neat idea!

choices.text: Did you two compete in the tournament?

talks.objective: Have a Genius Invokation TCG duel with Itto

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, Sara! We're looking for Kokomi, have you seen her anywhere?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I saw her exit the venue after the semifinals, but she hasn't returned since.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: If you're looking for Her Excellency, I believe she's currently near the western shore of Ritou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou! Good to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Hello, you two. Is there something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, we just wanted to say hello to Kokomi.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that I think about it, her opponent in the finals will be a tough one to beat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who are you rooting for, Sara?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Up till now, the Almighty Shogun had my full support. But now that she's been eliminated from the tournament... In truth, I don't really care.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought for sure that you'd be rooting for Miko.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I certainly would, in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: But now that the islands of Narukami and Watatsumi are on amiable terms, we're all friends.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Those are exactly Her Excellency's thoughts as well. The point of a game of cards between friends is to exchange skills and enjoy the game together. It's not about who wins or loses. She hopes that this spirit of friendly competition will define Inazuma going forward.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Hmm, a commendable attitude.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Her opponent is skilled in the art of deception. Even if she appears to have worry written all over her face, don't fall for it. She's likely trying to lead you into her trap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's nice to see two generals who were once enemies on the battlefield now looking out for each other.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Do not be mistaken. I speak only in the interests of fairness.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: The moment I saw the name "Sangonomiya" on the list of competitors, I anticipated that she would make it into the finals to face the Almighty Shogun.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I've watched every one of her matches. She constantly adapts her strategy, and excels at employing rare and unusual tactics.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: But after the Almighty Shogun's loss, I'm afraid that Lady Guuji may also have caught wind of Kokomi's strategies.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you wanna make sure Kokomi's got intel on the other side, too? Wow, trust Sara to make sure everything is fair and above board.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Thanks for your insights, General Kujou. I will be sure to pass them along to Her Excellency.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Don't mention it.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: The match will be starting shortly. Please let her know to get back to the venue soon.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Alright, then I'll get going.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Anyway, what are you two doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we were looking for Kokomi, have you seen her around?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or as Arataki "Numero Uno Idioso" so eloquently called her, "the fish lady."

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You're one to talk, Lavender Melon...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Her match in the finals will be starting shortly, so she can't be far.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Why don't you ask Kujou Sara over there? The Tenryou Commission is in charge of managing access to the venue and maintaining order.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, just remember that if you ever wanna play another match, you can find me anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kokomi!

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: #Paimon? Oh, and {NICKNAME}'s here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Surprised to see us? We came to wish you good luck in the competition!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what are you doing out here, Kokomi? Taking in the view?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, the soothing sound of the ocean's waves do make me feel peaceful, but I actually came here hoping to see Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Can you really see Watatsumi Island from here? Let Paimon take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Well? Can you see it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... That must be Kannazuka, and a little further than that, there's Yashiori Island... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, can't see Watatsumi.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Even on a perfectly clear day like this, you can't see Watatsumi Island from Narukami Island. Imagine trying to see it when the islands were surrounded by storms.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Though the islands are on peaceful terms now, the dark clouds of war still linger in some people's hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Even when friends argue, they still need time to reconcile. Think of how much time is needed when the conflicting sides could never even see each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You okay, Kokomi?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry... My mind was drifting to some more serious topics.

choices.text: You didn't join the tournament just to play cards...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Yes, I thought you might understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Who wins and who loses isn't what's most important.

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: What's important is that Her Excellency came here to compete with all of Inazuma watching.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Yes, more people will be traveling between Watatsumi and Narukami Island from this day forward.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: The point I hope to make is...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Even though we believe in different gods, we can all come together as friends by playing cards at the table. We should be willing to cooperate and assist one another in the future.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: You could say that I'm playing cards to help dissolve enmity.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're using a simple game of cards to drive major social change.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Yes, that's a good way to put it.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Besides, my passion has always been in tactics and strategy. How could I pass up the chance to play in a tournament for a strategic game like this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so you have your personal reasons to play, too.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Hehe. Yes, partly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You should be careful of that fox lady. Even Sara warned us that she'll be a cunning opponent.

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Yes. It seems that you're not the only one who sees this tournament as a chance to resolve our differences, Your Excellency.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Oh, that's good to hear.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon. I've already thought of a variety of stratagems for the match.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Paimon's really looking forward to the final now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon swears that she's actually gonna see it this time, no matter what! Paimon won't let herself get distracted, not even by all the tasty snacks in Inazuma!

choices.text: I'm also looking forward to it.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Thank you. Alright, let's go.

choices.text: You're competing for other reasons, too.

talks.objective: Return to the Ritou competition venue and attend the Final

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: "Inazuma's Archon Bolts Her Way to the Semifinals, Only to be Stunned by a Crafty Opponent"...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ooh, that's a nice title!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Lightning from Inazuma won't be able to reach me in Fontaine, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I don't think the Electro Archon would get upset over a minor thing like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you two chatting about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... the real question is, how many times are we gonna run into Kirara!?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Talk about a coincidence, right!? What are the chances!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I interviewed a few people around Ritou, but no more details on the Card Snatcher, unfortunately. After that, I ran into Kirara here. We got to chatting, and then I found out that she knew you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Sorry, you said "The Card Snatcher"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, let Paimon explain...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Paimon tells Kokomi everything that's happened recently...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Mm, I think I already have some insights regarding the truth of this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That fast!?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: But it's a little complicated, and the finals are about to start.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Let me put it this way, though. The key to this case...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Is actually Kirara.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, what...? Me!?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Having chatted with Kirara, I was starting to think the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Sorry, I don't have time to explain now. We'll have to continue after the tournament's finished.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just focus on your match, Kokomi.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... What should we do? Paimon's still trying to wrap her head around that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Kokomi was only working off of what Paimon told her, how come Paimon can't find the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Paimon really as dumb as a Lavender Melon?

choices.text: Don't worry about it, let's watch the competition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Oh, okay.

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: Welcome to the final round of the King of Invokations Grand Prix Inazuman regional final!

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: Our contestants are: Guuji Yae Miko of the Grand Narukami Shrine versus Sangonomiya Kokomi, Divine Priestess of the Sangonomiya Shrine!

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: Without further ado, let the final match begin!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, it's starting!

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: Now to find out who will play first!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You took your time. I was starting to wonder if you got lost walking on the seabed, Miss "Sole of the Deep."

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You must be tired after the walk back to shore. Perhaps I should let you go first?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: There's no need.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I've heard that "Fried Tofu With All the Frills" gets cold quickly. If you don't serve it right away, then I'm afraid it'll become a cold, greasy mess.

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: ...Round 1! Begin!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The two play a close and thrilling game of Genius Invokation...

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: And the winner is...

response.speaker: Master of Ceremonies
response.text: Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Divine Priestess from Watatsumi Island!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She won! Kokomi did it!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Whew, just seeing that kitsune youkai makes the fur on my tail stand on end.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kokomi! That was a real nail-biter, but you did it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That Miko is a crafty one! Pretending she had no strategy and letting one of her own character cards get defeated...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then she played two cards from her hand that required her to have lost a character card. She came pretty close to turning the match around!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Goodness, what's all the commotion over here? Discussing something interesting behind my back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! N—Not at all! P—Paimon was just saying what a real pity it was that you lost!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Haha, it's no pity at all. It was just a little fun competition.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: We'll see who wins next time. What do you say, Miss "Sole of the Deep"? How about a rematch?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: If Miss "Fried Tofu With All the Frills" hasn't gotten too cold, I would be happy to play.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #However, {NICKNAME} here is waiting for me to help them solve a puzzle they've been facing.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, really? Then I won't disturb you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'll go play with Gorou, instead. It's been a while since I've seen those fuzzy ears of his.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Ahem, now back to our conversation.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Kirara, you've been delivering items between different nations for the past several days, correct?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: That's right, I've had quite a few deliveries recently. But what does that have to do with the Card Snatcher?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: The strange thing is that Kirara's delivery route has coincided with the card snatcher's movements at every turn.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Yes, and therein lies the clue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... Kirara is the Card Snatcher!?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Huh? Hey, that's not true! I'm just out here doing my job! You can't just throw false accusations at a person... Ah, I mean a youkai like this!

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Calm down, you two. Kirara's not the thief.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Let me ask you, Kirara... Have any of your packages in the past few days been from the same sender? Or were any sent to the same destination?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Let me think... The senders have all been different. But there's one destination that keeps coming up, in every region I've been to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? And what destination is that?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Um... I'm not at liberty to give you the exact address, but I can tell you that it's in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Were the contents light? No larger than the size of an envelope?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Huh? Wait... You're not one of those youkai who has prophetic dreams, are you!? I used to hear stories about that when I was curled up on my grandma's lap...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Haha. No, I'm only the Divine Priestess of Watatsumi Island. I just like to read light novels and books about military strategy, divination's not my field.

choices.text: We can think about it later.

talks.objective: Deduce the truth with Kokomi's help

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, you nailed it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So the card backs we've been looking for have been right under our noses all along!?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But there's still one thing that doesn't quite add up.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Kirara picked up her package in Mondstadt before we encountered the Card Snatcher. The timing doesn't make sense.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I've thought about that, too. The way I see it, there's more than one thief involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So we're trailing not one, but multiple "card snatchers"?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, the person you've been tracking most likely is one member of the group.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: It seems the other members had already obtained the card backs and sent them together.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that I think about it, collecting all those card backs across so many nations would be near impossible for just one person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, why isn't the one we're following ever using Komaniya Express?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Because he's too slow. He probably missed the arranged shipment date. Well, that's how I figure it, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: From your explanation, he's only committed theft on one occasion, and there were even witnesses. After that, he's been trading or playing to collect the card backs.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I suspect that this person isn't a very good thief. He probably used the Mora he was given to arrange shipments with Komaniya Express as funds to use for trading.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Then there's another question now. Why don't the other members just keep the cards and take them back to Sumeru themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Unless... there's a reason for them to stay...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, this is a question I'm still grappling with now.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: What is the thieves' objective? What kind of secret is hidden behind these card backs?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, there's no way to know without seeing one for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: H—Hey, don't look at me like that! I can't just open a customer's parcel!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: If the company ever found out, I'd be fired on the spot!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: And I don't want to go back to being a youkai in the mountains of Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: No, we don't want to cause you any trouble, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: At this point... Mm, maybe it would be best for you all to accompany Kirara to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea! Going to the delivery location is the only lead worth following now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And if the recipient really is a bad guy, then Kirara could be in danger. We should come along to make sure you're safe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can beat up bad guys.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hey, I know my way around a fight, too! I haven't had a single package stolen from me since I've started this job!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Whenever someone picks on me thinking I'd be an easy target to take packages from, I send them running!

choices.text: I'm still concerned about your safety...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Hmm, let me think about it...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Alright, I'll let you come with me to the delivery point in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: But, on one condition!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: You have to promise that you'll hide somewhere where the customer can't see you. Who's ever heard of a group of people delivering packages?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem, you got it!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Also, even if the customer is a bad guy and has stolen things, we should leave that for the local authorities to handle.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Absolutely.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next stop, Sumeru! We're really traveling all over the place this time.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Good luck. You'll have to tell me how everything turns out the next time we meet.

choices.text: We have to get to the bottom of this mystery...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Well? After all I've said so far, have you arrived at the same answer as me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I accept your challenge.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Great! See? This is what I call a true compadre! Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alright, I'll be the judge, then.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Just remember to take it easy, you two. This isn't a high-stakes match. It really doesn't matter who wins or loses.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Shush! Do you guys hear that? It's the cry of my cards, cheering me on in the wind!

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: ...MY cards, you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got other things to do right now...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ah, really? Alright, well, some other time then.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Just come find me whenever you have some time to play!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we were looking for Kokomi, have you seen her around?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or as Arataki "Numero Uno Idioso" so eloquently called her, "the fish lady."

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You're one to talk, Lavender Melon...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Her match in the finals will be starting shortly, so she can't be far.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Why don't you ask Kujou Sara over there? The Tenryou Commission is in charge of managing access to the venue and maintaining order.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: ...Mkay, but don't forget about your compadre here, alright? I'll be waiting for ya!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Huh, I can't believe I lost.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: And I can't believe your deck won. That takes some serious skill.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hahaha! See, my theory was correct!

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Don't let it get to you... You were using Boss's deck, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Miko... The people of Inazuma are afraid of me...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: And for good reason, no? A bolt of lightning from you would make even my fur stand on end.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: You know I would never do such a thing...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Nor would I eat anyone! Yet, a writer of mine seems convinced that I'd turn into an evil kitsune and eat him alive if he doesn't submit his drafts on time. Honestly, where do people get these ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, although to be fair, after I learned that he was afraid of me, I did start acting like I might actually eat him. Needless to say, his punctuality is now improving with each draft.

dialogues.speaker: Qiuyue
dialogues.text: The Almighty Shogun herself has come to Ritou to compete in the King of Invokations Grand Prix.

dialogues.speaker: Qiuyue
dialogues.text: How blessed we are. Her presence here today is sure to boost business in Ritou for a long time to come.

dialogues.speaker: Vahid
dialogues.text: Oh, if only I'd thought ahead, I could have sponsored the King of Invokations Grand Prix with my Anahitian Blessing. This could've been the perfect promotional opportunity for me!

dialogues.speaker: Vahid
dialogues.text: Hmm, although on second thought... Who'd wanna win a bunch of fertilizer as a prize? ...*sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Karpillia
dialogues.text: Is that the Electro Archon? You definitely don't see her every day.

dialogues.speaker: Karpillia
dialogues.text: Huh, now that I think about it, I've actually never seen the Anemo Archon, either.

dialogues.speaker: Karpillia
dialogues.text: Eh, but that doesn't matter. May the Anemo Archon continue to bring my business the winds of success.

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: Is that really the Almighty Shogun?

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: Huh... None of the figurines I sell in the shop come close to capturing her in all her glory.

dialogues.speaker: Kaede
dialogues.text: Maybe it's time to release a new one...

dialogues.speaker: Xixi
dialogues.text: Everybody's been playing that card game lately... Maybe I should learn how to play? *sigh* But it'd take so much mental energy, it'd probably only make me even sleepier.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: The Almighty Shogun's TCG skills were truly amazing to witness. She beat me fair and square.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Times have taken a turn for the better now. I'm sure that under the Almighty Shogun's rule, brighter days lie ahead for the International Trade Association.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: What's up, compadre! You here to play another game?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: You've got it! This oni's ready to play all day!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: No worries, you go do what you gotta do. I'll see ya later.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, compadre! How about a game? You versus me!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: *sigh* Alright, I'll be the judge, then.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Just remember to take it easy, you two. This isn't a high-stakes match. It really doesn't matter who wins or loses.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Shush! Do you guys hear that? It's the cry of my cards, cheering me on in the wind!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: ...MY cards, you mean.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: No problem! Arataki "The Ultimate TCG Champion" Itto never backs down from a challenge, I'll be waitin'.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I hope the final goes smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Everything should be fine... as long as that oni manages to avoid causing a scene.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Every nation Kirara visited had a parcel sent to Sumeru...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The contents were light, and were no larger than an envelope...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The contents were probably Genius Invokation cards...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We've run into Kirara multiple times throughout our trip...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We came to Inazuma because we tracked the thief here...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The thief is likely using Komaniya Express to send packages...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Kirara's deliveries contain the treasure chest card backs!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...No, that doesn't seem to be the answer...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hmm, there doesn't seem to be any more leads...)
